Understanding Tax Lien Certificates

Tax lien certificates are a powerful investment tool. When a property owner fails to pay their taxes, the county can place a lien on the property and sell it at auction. Investors purchase these liens, essentially paying the property owner’s tax debt in exchange for the right to collect that debt, plus interest, from the owner. If the owner does not pay within the redemption period, the investor can initiate foreclosure proceedings to take ownership of the property.

Steps to Start Investing

Research and Understand Local Laws

Understanding the legal framework is crucial. Boone County follows Illinois state laws, which include a 2.5-year redemption period and interest rates that can reach up to 18% annually.

Visit the Local Treasurer’s Website

Check the Boone County Treasurer’s Office for detailed information about upcoming auctions and registration requirements.

Check the Auction Site

Auctions are held at the County Board room at the Boone County Administration Campus.

Read the Details About Tax Liens

Make sure to understand the sale schedule, parcel inquiries, and any other essential details provided on the Treasurer’s website.

Contact the County Office

For additional inquiries, contact the Boone County Treasurer’s Office at 815-544-2666.

Pro Tips

  • Register Early: Ensure your registration and deposit are submitted on time.
  • Research Properties: Investigate the properties thoroughly before bidding.
  • Consult Legal Advice: Consider consulting with an attorney to navigate the complexities of tax lien investing.

FAQs

When and where is the next tax sale?

The next tax sale is expected to be on October at 1212 Logan Avenue, Belvidere, IL 61008, in the County Board room.

Do I need to register for the sale?

Yes, all buyers must register with a $250 fee at least two weeks before the sale.

Can I bid without attending?

No, you must be physically present to bid, as the auction uses an open outcry format.

What happens if the property owner redeems the lien?

You will receive your initial investment plus interest accrued.
